reader.requirement: At --std 85 a bare OBJECT-COMPUTER header (the whole bracketed entry, computer-name included, omitted) must be accepted and the program run on the implementor's object computer, which DOC-A.1-126 documents as the one .NET runtime with the native collating sequence; the second period without an entry and a clause without computer-name lie outside the 1985 format and must be refused.

reader.notes: The grammar makes computer-name and clauses optional; VersionConformancePass refuses only the 2002 relaxations. The implementor definition is DOC-A.1-126 (one object computer, native sequence), and the bare header binds no Collating, so ObjectComputerEmit emits no __COLLATE and comparisons use the native order.

refuter.evidence: r44a-002: OBJECT-COMPUTER. header with no entry, followed directly by INPUT-OUTPUT SECTION (no SOURCE-COMPUTER, no SPECIAL-NAMES) at --std 85 compiles and runs: LOW-VALUE < 'Z' < 'a' < HIGH-VALUE holds (native order, DOC-A.1-126) and a SORT with no COLLATING SEQUENCE returns 1, Z, a (native).
